answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce deposit before it may vote or claim rewards. When several identities coordinate, a public challenge can expose shared control; proven duplicates lose their deposits, while honest agents keep theirs. The loss creates a ripple through an attacker’s budget: each extra persona needs more capital at risk, not merely another email address. A cipher can protect private credentials, and a lantern can signal suspicious clusters, but neither replaces the deposit’s direct economic cost.
